text: Epiphenomenalism about the mental (associated with T.H. Huxley) is the view that:
choices: Mental events are strictly identical to brain events
Mentality is the only reality, and matter is an illusion
Mental and physical events are perfectly synchronized by God
Physical events cause mental events, but mental events themselves cause nothing — they are causally inert byproducts
explanation: Epiphenomenalism holds that phenomenal/mental events are caused by physical processes but are themselves causally impotent — like steam from an engine that drives nothing. Option 0 is the identity theory; option 1 is idealism; option 2 is occasionalism/pre-established harmony. What is distinctive is the one-way causal arrow from physical to mental.
